entities.name: Theodotus of Antioch
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Theodotus of Antioch, Patriarch of Antioch (417-429 CE), played a pivotal role in reconciling the long-standing schism of Meletius at Antioch and following Alexander of Antioch's lead in replacing the honoured name of John Chrysostom on the diptychs of the church.

As Patriarch, Theodotus oversaw the reunification of the Eastern Orthodox Church under the authority of the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, thereby bridging the theological divide between the 'Alexandrian' and 'Antiochenian' schools of thought.

This event had significant regional implications, as Theodotus's successor, Peter III, continued to consolidate power in Antioch, solidifying the city's position as a crucial hub of early Christian theology and practice.

Theodotus's legacy extended beyond the regional scope, as his actions contributed to the eventual reunification of the Eastern Orthodox Church under the Ecumenical Patriarchate, a development that would have far-reaching consequences for the development of Christianity in the Eastern Mediterranean.

One striking testament to Theodotus's enduring impact is the preservation of his legacy through the writings of the Byzantine historian Theophanes the Confessor, who cited Theodotus as a key figure in the reunification of the Church.
